mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0 and remains elevated for three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over six months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for six consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of six-month RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of four-month INDPRO outperformance (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which reduces macroeconomic uncertainty and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL falls over three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS rise and CPIAUCSL decline (t-test p > 0.05).
